summary: Gifford Pinchot NF summit cabin: D-6 cupola built 1918, staffed about 1921-1924, now usually buried in snow and ice. NHLR-registered 2009.

facts.design: 12 by 12 foot wood-frame D-6 cupola ground cabin with a quarter-size second-story cupola; two lean-to additions from the 1932 sulfur mining
facts.status_note: Structure remains on the summit but is usually entombed in snow and ice; visible only for a few weeks in dry late summers.

access.note: On the summit of Mount Adams, reached only by a long mountaineering climb. No managed access, permit or rental is described in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Reached only by climbing Mount Adams. TrailChick says even the least technical route can require an ice axe, crampons and mountaineering gear, and conditions change rapidly. The cabin is usually buried in snow and ice.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and TrailChick give 1918 as the build year. firelookout.com says construction began in 1918 and continued three years. troutlake.org says construction ran from 1920 to 1921. TrailChick says the lookout was completed in 1922. The story gives 1918 as the start and reports 1921 and 1922 as completion dates.

NHLR and TrailChick give service from 1921 to 1924. firelookout.com gives 1922-1924. TrailChick says retired 1925; troutlake.org says the decision to abandon came in 1924. The story gives about 1921 to 1924.

NHLR and firelookout.com put the miners in the early 1930s (NHLR says 1932). troutlake.org says a company formed in 1929 to propose mining. The story uses the early 1930s for occupation and does not date the company.

notes_for_editor: Build and staffing dates conflict across four sources; all are reported in the story. Current condition is from a 2018 blog visit and a 2019 NHLR visit report. Contains route-safety advice only; does not encourage the climb. Visit reports on NHLR are the only source for staffing status. Search budget: one WebSearch used.
